industry: Railcar manufacturing (N. America, Mexico, Europe, Brazil JV), leasing (~15,500 owned fleet), maintenance services
drawdown_context: GBX entered the 2025-05-15 cutoff at $47.28 after a -33% drawdown from its trailing 52-week high. Tape pressure was driven by (i) cyclical concerns over softer freight-railcar order cycle (backlog $3.81B 8/31/23 to $3.38B 8/31/24 to $3.0B 11/30/24 to $2.6B 2/28/25), (ii) the new U.S. administration tariff agenda directly threatening Greenbrier's Mexican manufacturing footprint (~half of 14,200 employees in Mexico; GIMSA 50/50 JV at Frontera Mexico is the primary North American railcar manufacturing platform), and (iii) general industrial multiple compression. The drawdown was an external/cyclical/policy-uncertainty event, NOT a disclosed distress event. FY24 (year ended 8/31/24) financials were UP materially: net earnings attributable to Greenbrier $160.1M vs $62.5M (+156%), EPS diluted $4.96 vs $1.89, margin 15.8% vs 11.2%. Q1 FY25 (11/30/24) and Q2 FY25 (2/28/25) both grew earnings YoY (+77% and +55%).

summary: GBX is a textbook honesty-alpha PASS into a cyclical/policy-uncertainty drawdown. Across three pre-cutoff filings (FY24 10-K 10/24/2024, Q1 FY25 10-Q 1/10/2025, Q2 FY25 10-Q 4/8/2025) management behavior is anti-correlated with every Mode B distress tell. Net earnings attributable to Greenbrier grew +156% YoY in FY24 ($62.5M to $160.1M) on revenue DOWN -10% (real margin expansion 11.2% to 15.8%), and grew +77% (Q1 FY25) and +55% (Q2 FY25) into the drawdown window. Quarterly dividend was RAISED to $0.32 on April 1 2025 -- Board-level signal made AFTER tariff threats were already pressuring the stock -- and the $100M share repurchase authorization was EXPANDED and EXTENDED on January 8 2025 (from $45.1M/Jan-2025 expiry to fresh $100M/Jan-2027) but NOT executed (zero shares repurchased across entire pre-cutoff window). KPMG (Big-4, 13-year tenure) clean ICFR opinion is genuine, with FY23 ITGC material weakness around new ERP fully REMEDIATED during FY24 and held remediated across Q1 and Q2 FY25 certifications. Customer concentration is IMPROVING across the 3-year window (FY22 top-3 = 39% combined to FY24 top-1 = 10%). CFO transition (Adrian Downes to Michael Donfris) was structured 16+ months ahead of cutoff, with outgoing CFO consulting fee REDUCED on extension (April 4 2025 amendment to nominal $1,000/month) -- opposite of hush-money. Only ONE 10b5-1 plan adoption in entire pre-cutoff window (Krueger COO 10,892 shares adopted July 2024 pre-catalyst); zero in Q1 or Q2 FY25 (no insider flight). 2024 convertible notes retired on schedule in cash ($47.7M Feb 2024). Backlog rolldown (30,900 to 20,400 units; $3.81B to $2.6B) orderly with stable per-unit revenue (~$127K), no silent mix degradation. Liquidity at 2/28/25 was ~$750M ($263.5M cash + $488.0M available borrowings). Single yellow flag: QUALITATIVE-only Mexico tariff disclosure (GIMSA 50/50 JV at Frontera, ~7,100 Mexican employees) -- risk explicitly flagged in 10-K Item 1A and Q2 FY25 MD&A but no quantified tariff-sensitivity scenario. Moderate underdelivery of specificity, not deception. Composite should land in deep PASS range (~0.15), validating framework as false-positive guardrail. Forward return +1.4% confirms call: GBX survived the year without distress.
